name: Greenish pistachio

sections.title: Greenish pistachio is a bright yellow-green carried into our library from the Japanese traditional color Usumo'egi, "pale young green onion," and it sits 6.0 units from the plain [[pistachio]].
sections.body:
Our library lists this color under the Japanese name Usumo'egi, written 淡萌黄, glossed as "pale young green onion" [1]. The first element, *usu*, means pale or thin, and *moegi* names the bright green of a sprouting onion or leek shoot [1]. No book consulted independently dates the coinage beyond that library gloss, so it is undocumented here [1].

The swatch measures lightness 68, chroma 51 and hue 123 degrees, in the Greens family, used chiefly in fashion and textile contexts [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[neva-green]], [[asparagus]], [[nasty-green]] and [[leaf]], at 4.4, 4.5, 5 and 5.3 ΔE [1]. A darker member of the same batch of traditional names is [[greenish-umber]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within range of this swatch appears in 19 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.08 percent, as photographed, mostly as a highlight rather than a shadow [2]. The earliest dated match is Salomon van Ruysdael's 1652 *The Road along the River*, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. The archive's photographs are of aged, varnished canvases, so a match is a nearby screen color, not a pigment identification [2].
